findings.issue_text: [BUG] uploads_controller.rb:65-69 downsize loop passes literal "80%" as dimensions, but animated GIF branch (downsize_instructions_animated) parses dimensions with split('x') and does arithmetic, causing NoMethodError/TypeError on the nil height component and a 500 that discards the downloaded tempfile

[BUG] utilities.js:182 hardcodes maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignoring SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, causing false rejections of valid uploads on sites with larger limits and letting oversized files through on sites with smaller limits

[ADVISORY] optimized_image.rb:145-147 self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) is immediately redefined by self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) in the same class body, leaving dead code that confuses maintainers

[ADVISORY] uploads_controller.rb:55 FileHelper.download hardcodes a 10MB download cap for API URL imports, ignoring SiteSetting.max_attachment_size_kb/max_image_size_kb, so legitimately-sized imports silently fail via rescue nil

[ADVISORY] uploads_controller.rb:65-69 retry loop runs OptimizedImage.downsize up to 5 times without checking convert_with return value or breaking on failure/success, and proceeds to Upload.create_for even when the file still exceeds max_image_size_kb, wasting CPU and yielding confusing errors

[BUG] `downsize` in app/models/optimized_image.rb:142-152 is defined twice; the second definition shadows the first, breaking existing two-argument callers with a TypeError (avatar/thumbnail generation crashes on every existing downsize call site)

[BUG] In uploads_controller.rb:63-68, the animated-GIF branch is dead code because `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` matches a Tempfile path with no extension, so animated GIFs over the size limit are downsized to a single frozen frame

[BUG] The downsize loop caps at 5 iterations of '80%' without verifying the file reached `max_image_size_kb`, so large PNGs can still exceed the limit and fail with a 'file too large' error after 5 wasted ImageMagick runs

[BUG] The client-side cap in utilities.js:182 is hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring the `max_image_size_kb` site setting, so admins raising the limit see users still blocked at 10MB and the 413 error reports the wrong limit

[ADVISORY] The API URL-download branch in uploads_controller.rb:56 hardcodes `10.megabytes`, desynchronizing from `max_image_size_kb` and causing silent truncation/failure of URL-based API uploads above 10MB

[ADVISORY] No tests cover the new server-side downsize loop, including oversized-image acceptance, animated GIF handling, the 5-iteration failure mode, and the `downsize` signature change, leaving no regression net on a user-facing upload path

[ADVISORY] `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` gates downsizing on the client-supplied/URL-derived filename extension, so oversized files with non-image extensions skip downsizing entirely and get the old hard failure

[BUG] The downsize loop running OptimizedImage.downsize at most 5 times with "80%" scaling does not monotonically reduce file size; after 5 attempts the tempfile can still exceed SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb and Upload.create_for proceeds anyway, so large-image uploads still fail with the original error after 5 expensive imagemagick invocations blocking the request.

[BUG] OptimizedImage.downsize is defined twice (once with max_width, max_height, once with dimensions); Ruby does not support overloading, so the second definition replaces the first and pre-existing call sites passing width and height separately now break — binding height into opts, producing broken optimized-image generation and TypeError crash paths.

[BUG] maxSizeKB is hardcoded to 10 * 1024 for all types in utilities.js, but only images get server-side downsizing; non-image types still enforce their (possibly smaller) server-side limit, so users uploading attachments above the site's configured limit pass the client check but get rejected server-side with a 413.

[ADVISORY] Scope drift: replacing the SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] lookup with a hardcoded constant removes administrator configurability for every upload type; the requirement could be met by only relaxing the image client check, leaving other types' settings intact.

[ADVISORY] FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...) for API-provided URLs caps downloads at a hardcoded 10MB regardless of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, causing spurious download failures for in-limit images on sites with large-image settings; the cap should derive from the site setting.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop overwrites tempfile.path in place, so if 5 attempts fail the user's original image data is destroyed and a degraded (80%^5 ≈ 33% linear scale) image is what Upload.create_for receives; users lose fidelity with no indication or undo.

[ADVISORY] Coverage gap: the new controller branch (animated-image behavior under allow_animation, the 5-attempt loop, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb == 0 skip, non-image passthrough, API-URL-download path) has no tests, and no regression test verifies OptimizedImage.downsize's changed signature against existing optimized-image generation.

[ADVISORY] FileHelper.is_image?(filename) relies on filename, which for the API-URL branch is File.basename(URI.parse(url).path); extension-less URLs (common for signed/CDN URLs) are not detected as images, skip downsizing, and then fail the size check — the content type should be used as the discriminator instead.

[BUG] Ruby does not support method overloading; the new three-argument `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` completely replaces the four-argument version defined three lines above it, so existing callers passing width and height separately now get `dimensions = 100` (an Integer) and `opts = 200`, causing `downsize_instructions` to receive an Integer where it expects a "WxH" geometry string, breaking ImageMagick commands and thumbnail generation across the optimized-image pipeline

[BUG] `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%")` passes a percentage, but downscaling by 80% of dimensions is not guaranteed to reduce file size below `max_image_size_kb`, so the loop can exhaust all 5 attempts and fall through to `Upload.create_for` with a still-oversized file, failing with a size error the user was told wouldn't happen

[ADVISORY] Client-side max-size precheck in utilities.js:182 & 246 is hardcoded to 10 * 1024 KB for every upload type, while the server enforces per-type SiteSetting limits, so users on types whose setting is below 10MB lose the friendly pre-validation and admins' setting changes stop taking effect client-side; the universal-ceiling rebuttal fails for non-image types where no downsizing occurs due to the `is_image?` gate

[ADVISORY] The downsizing loop in uploads_controller.rb:66-69 has no check on whether the file actually shrank: if `convert_with` fails (ImageMagick error leaves the tempfile untouched), the loop re-runs the identical failing command 4 more times with no effect, then proceeds with the original oversized file, wasting 5x full-process re-encode cost on the request path

[ADVISORY] The auto-downsize path in uploads_controller.rb:65 applies only to this controller entry point, but `Upload.create_for` is called from several other paths (other controllers, background jobs, onebox/import code) that keep the old reject-oversized behavior, making the feature path-dependent and inconsistent

[ADVISORY] `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` on the URL branch in uploads_controller.rb:63 is decided by the URL's basename extension, so extension-less URLs or content-mismatched extensions misclassify the file, skipping downsizing for perfectly downsizable images; a content-type sniff on the downloaded tempfile would be the faithful discriminator

[BUG] app/models/optimized_image.rb:142-160: `def self.downsize` is defined twice in the same module with different signatures (4-arg `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` vs 3/4-arg `(from, to, dimensions, opts)`); the second definition replaces the first in Ruby, so existing 4-argument call sites pass `max_height` as the `dimensions` string and existing downsizing paths crash or produce broken geometry

[BUG] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-68: shrink loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` with the same path as both `from` and `to`, an in-place convert hazard that can leave the tempfile truncated/destroyed

[BUG] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-68: the loop ignores the `false` return value of `convert_with` and re-runs `downsize` up to 5 times even after a failed convert, so a corrupt/non-convertible image (e.g. mislabeled content-type) passes the still-oversized tempfile to `Upload.create_for`, yielding a server 500/422 instead of a friendly size error

[BUG] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182: client-side upload validation hardcodes `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024`, discarding `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` / `max_attachment_size_kb`; sites with smaller limits accept files client-side that the server rejects, including oversized non-image attachments, producing raw server errors instead of the pre-upload `file_too_large` message

[BUG] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246: the 413 handler hardcodes 10MB, so on any site whose `max_image_size_kb` differs from 10240 the error message states a wrong limit for that site, producing confusing, non-actionable messages

[BUG] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:56: the API/URL download path hardcodes `10.megabytes`, ignoring `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`; it runs before the downsize loop, so remote images over 10MB silently fail download (`rescue nil` → `tempfile = nil`) with no size-specific error, bypassing the admin-configured limit and behaving inconsistently with the browser flow

[ADVISORY] app/models/optimized_image.rb:143-155: intent drift without acceptance — the refactor from `(width, height)` to a `dimensions` string changes the long-standing internal API contract while `resize` keeps `(from, to, width, height)` and formats `"#{width}x#{height}"` internally (two conventions in adjacent methods), and the deleted `dimensions()` helper breaks any remaining callers; passing a "WxH" string to `resize` silently produces broken geometry like "WxHx"

[ADVISORY] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-68: the unconditional 5-iteration shell-out downsize loop runs on the synchronous upload request path; repeated ImageMagick invocations on large images (e.g. 20MB animated GIFs with `allow_animation`) can take tens of seconds per upload, causing request-thread saturation and upload timeouts affecting all users of that web process

[ADVISORY] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65-67: the new behavior-bearing downsize loop (attempt counter, `allow_animation` gating, "80%" step size, post-loop size compliance) has zero test coverage, so regressions like the double-`def downsize` bug or "80%" never shrinking below `max_image_size_kb` would ship undetected and the feature's core promise is unverifiable

[BUG] app/models/optimized_image.rb:144-152 — `def self.downsize` is defined twice in the same module body; Ruby keeps only the last definition, so the 4-arg signature at line 144 is dead code and callers passing separate width/height hit a different 4-arg signature where `max_width` alone is used as the dimensions string, sending a bare number like "690" into `downsize_instructions`, producing width-only geometry that mis-sizes thumbnails and avatars site-wide

[ADVISORY] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-70 — downsizing loop caps at 5 iterations of 80% (~32.8% reduction), so uploads just over the limit (e.g. 4× max_image_size_kb) still exceed the setting when the loop exits and `Upload.create_for` is called with an oversized tempfile, causing silent, inconsistent behavior for images between ~3× and 4× the limit with no error surfaced

[ADVISORY] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with hardcoded `10 * 1024` makes the client-side gate ignore admin-configured per-type limits, and the i18n message always reports "10 MB" regardless of what the server enforces, creating a mismatch between promised and enforced policy; the 413 handler at utilities.js:246 also always claims 10MB even for other configured limits

[ADVISORY] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:56 — the `FileHelper.download(url, ...)` call raises its cap from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to hardcoded `10.megabytes` while the URL remains unvalidated (no scheme/host/private-IP check), allowing API clients to make the server fetch 10MB from any URL including internal addresses, widening SSRF exposure and exfiltration window

[ADVISORY] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` gates the downsize path on the attacker-controlled user-supplied filename extension, while `allow_animation` inside `optimize` gates on `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` against the server-generated tempfile path; the two checks use different name sources, enabling media-type confusion reaching the shell-invoked convert path and causing animated GIFs disguised with non-.GIF extensions to skip the animated-instruction branch

[BUG] app/models/optimized_image.rb:~143-153 — duplicate `def self.downsize` method definition; Ruby silently overwrites the first definition, and callers passing width+height numerically hit the second definition where `height` lands in the `opts` slot, causing `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer`

[BUG] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64-69 — the downsizing loop (5 iterations of 80%) cannot guarantee files get under max_image_size_kb; loop exits with file still over the limit and `Upload.create_for` rejects it, failing for exactly the inputs the feature targets, with no error handling for the 'still too large' outcome

[ADVISORY] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — in-place `downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` risks a truncated/corrupt tempfile on failed ImageMagick runs, and the return value of `convert_with` (false on exitstatus != 0) is ignored, so a broken convert looks identical to success

[ADVISORY] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 and :246 — hard-coding `10 * 1024` in place of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` silently overrides admin configuration and drops the type distinction (avatar/composer/other limits previously separate settings); admins who lower max_image_size_kb get a client that accepts files the server rejects, and admins who raise it above 10MB see uploads blocked at 10MB

[ADVISORY] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:243-248 — I18n interpolation uses a hardcoded value while the server's actual rejection threshold is `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`; the 413 message tells users 'max size is 10240 KB' regardless of the server's configured limit, misstating the policy on non-default installs

[BUG] OptimizedImage.downsize is defined twice in optimized_image.rb:143-149; the second 3-arg def silently replaces the original 4-arg version, causing ArgumentError for all existing 4-arg callers (avatar/thumbnail/cooked-image resizing paths crash at runtime)

[BUG] The downsize loop in uploads_controller.rb:63-70 calls OptimizedImage.downsize with from == to, destructively overwriting the user's uploaded original in place with no backup; the original full-resolution data is irreversibly lost, and a partial ImageMagick failure can leave a truncated/corrupt file with nothing stored

[BUG] The '80%' geometry in the downsize loop reduces dimensions by 20% per pass, so images can still exceed max_image_size_kb after all 5 attempts, then Upload.create_for is called with an oversized file that fails validation after wasted CPU passes (or gets stored oversized)

[ADVISORY] Hardcoded 10 * 1024 KB client-side and 10.megabytes server-side replace SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb in utilities.js:182, utilities.js:246, and uploads_controller.rb:55, silently ignoring the admin-configurable setting and causing the limits to disagree within the same diff

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop's animated-GIF handling depends on the tempfile path ending in .GIF, but tempfile paths never end in .gif, so the animated instructions branch can never trigger and large animated GIFs get flattened/handled as static images, destroying animation

[BUG] `app/models/optimized_image.rb:145-156` — `def self.downsize` is defined twice in the same class; Ruby keeps the later definition, so callers passing the old 4-parameter signature `(from, to, max_width, max_height)` have the 4th argument (`height`) bound to `opts`, causing `opts[:allow_animation]` to raise `TypeError (no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer)` and crashing every thumbnail/lightbox path that downsizes with explicit width/height.

[BUG] `app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-68` — `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` passes the literal string `"80%"` as the `dimensions` argument into `downsize_instructions`/`downsize_instructions_animated`, which expect width/height geometry; the malformed convert command fails, `convert_with` returns `false` which is discarded, all 5 loop attempts run against an unchanged file, and `Upload.create_for` receives the original oversized tempfile with no indication of downsizing failure.

[BUG] `app/assets/javascripts/utilities.js:182` — `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB` replaces the per-type server setting `SiteSetting['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, so admin-configured limits are ignored client-side: uploads the server would accept are blocked at 10MB, files between the real server limit and 10MB pass client validation and hit a 413, and the error message at line 246 always states "10 MB" regardless of the actual enforced limit.

[ADVISORY] `app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55` — `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` hardcodes the URL-download cap for all types including attachments, ignoring `max_attachment_size_kb`; for large image URLs the download is silently truncated via `rescue nil` and `Upload.create_for` is called with `tempfile == nil`, causing `tempfile.size` to raise NoMethodError and return a 500 instead of a 4xx response.

[ADVISORY] `app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64-68` — Up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick invocations run inline on the request thread with no timeout, discarded output, and in-place read/write on the same tempfile path; a pathological or adversarial large image can pin a web worker for the duration of 5 unbounded converts, and the API/URL path can reach this loop with arbitrarily large remote files despite the client-side 10MB cap.

[ADVISORY] `app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-68` — The downsize loop's only exit conditions are `attempt == 0` or size satisfied, with no distinction between progress and failure; when 5 iterations of 80% scaling still leave the file above `max_image_size_kb`, the code silently proceeds to upload creation which fails size validation, giving the user a confusing "file too large" error with no indication downsizing was attempted and no log line recording the failure.

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] uploads_controller.rb:65-69 downsize loop passes literal "80%" as dimensions, but animated GIF branch (downsize_instructions_animated) parses dimensions with split('x') and does arithmetic, causing NoMethodError/TypeError on the nil height component and a 500 that discards the downloaded tempfile

[BUG] utilities.js:182 hardcodes maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignoring SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, causing false rejections of valid uploads on sites with larger limits and letting oversized files through on sites with smaller limits

[ADVISORY] optimized_image.rb:145-147 self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) is immediately redefined by self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) in the same class body, leaving dead code that confuses maintainers

[ADVISORY] uploads_controller.rb:55 FileHelper.download hardcodes a 10MB download cap for API URL imports, ignoring SiteSetting.max_attachment_size_kb/max_image_size_kb, so legitimately-sized imports silently fail via rescue nil

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb#create_upload`, the API URL import path changed from `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` to `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`, hardcoding a 10MB limit and no longer honoring the configured `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (and by extension any attachment/image size settings). The `rescue nil` also means oversize/failed downloads can be swallowed, matching the finding’s concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] uploads_controller.rb:65-69 retry loop runs OptimizedImage.downsize up to 5 times without checking convert_with return value or breaking on failure/success, and proceeds to Upload.create_for even when the file still exceeds max_image_size_kb, wasting CPU and yielding confusing errors

adjudication.rationale: The new loop in uploads_controller.rb (attempt=5; while attempt>0 && tempfile.size > max) calls OptimizedImage.downsize(...) repeatedly without checking whether the conversion succeeded (convert_with can return false) and will still proceed to Upload.create_for even if the file remains over the limit after 5 tries. The loop does stop when size drops below the limit via its condition, so it won’t always run 5 times, but failure cases can waste CPU and lead to later, less clear upload errors rather than an explicit failure here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `downsize` in app/models/optimized_image.rb:142-152 is defined twice; the second definition shadows the first, breaking existing two-argument callers with a TypeError (avatar/thumbnail generation crashes on every existing downsize call site)

[BUG] In uploads_controller.rb:63-68, the animated-GIF branch is dead code because `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` matches a Tempfile path with no extension, so animated GIFs over the size limit are downsized to a single frozen frame

adjudication.rationale: The new downsizing loop in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, ...)` with `allow_animation: ...`. In `optimized_image.rb`, the animated branch selection is `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, i.e. it relies on the *file path* having a `.gif` extension. A `Tempfile` path (especially for URL downloads via `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`) typically won’t end with `.gif`, so the `_animated` instructions won’t be used even when the original `filename` is a GIF. That can cause animated GIFs to be processed via the non-animated path (potentially losing animation), matching the finding’s concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The downsize loop caps at 5 iterations of '80%' without verifying the file reached `max_image_size_kb`, so large PNGs can still exceed the limit and fail with a 'file too large' error after 5 wasted ImageMagick runs

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a best-effort downsizing loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that runs at most 5 times while `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", ...)`. It is true this does not guarantee the file will end up under `max_image_size_kb` (e.g., some formats/compression characteristics), so the upload may still fail later after multiple ImageMagick runs. However, this is an efficiency/edge-case limitation of the new “auto-reduce” feature, not a clear correctness defect: if it doesn’t shrink enough, the system will still reject the upload as before, just with extra work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The client-side cap in utilities.js:182 is hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring the `max_image_size_kb` site setting, so admins raising the limit see users still blocked at 10MB and the 413 error reports the wrong limit

[ADVISORY] The API URL-download branch in uploads_controller.rb:56 hardcodes `10.megabytes`, desynchronizing from `max_image_size_kb` and causing silent truncation/failure of URL-based API uploads above 10MB

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the API URL-download path in `uploads_controller.rb` from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes` (`tempfile = FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`). This makes URL-based API uploads fail/be rejected once the remote file exceeds 10MB, even if the site setting `max_image_size_kb` is configured higher. The new downsize loop that follows can only run if the full file is downloaded, so this hard cap can prevent the intended “download big then downsize to allowed size” behavior for API URL uploads above 10MB.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] No tests cover the new server-side downsize loop, including oversized-image acceptance, animated GIF handling, the 5-iteration failure mode, and the `downsize` signature change, leaving no regression net on a user-facing upload path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial, user-facing upload behavior in `UploadsController#create_upload` (a 5-try loop calling `OptimizedImage.downsize` to shrink oversized images, with GIF/animation behavior gated by `allow_animated_thumbnails`) and also changes `OptimizedImage`’s `downsize/optimize` API to take a single `dimensions` argument (and adjusts `resize/downsize` to pass strings like "#{w}x#{h}"). This PR diff does not include any accompanying test changes to cover these new paths (oversized-image acceptance via downsizing, animated GIF branch selection, the 5-iteration failure mode, and the signature change), making it a concrete, diff-grounded risk rather than a generic 'add tests' request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` gates downsizing on the client-supplied/URL-derived filename extension, so oversized files with non-image extensions skip downsizing entirely and get the old hard failure

adjudication.rationale: The new server-side downsizing block in `UploadsController#create_upload` is gated by `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`, where `filename` comes from `file.original_filename` or the URL path basename. That means an actually-image upload with a misleading/non-image extension would skip the downsizing loop and then proceed to `Upload.create_for(...)` without being reduced, likely resulting in the pre-existing “too large” rejection based on `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. This is a concrete edge-case limitation introduced by the new logic, but not necessarily a general defect for normal/valid image uploads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The downsize loop running OptimizedImage.downsize at most 5 times with "80%" scaling does not monotonically reduce file size; after 5 attempts the tempfile can still exceed SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb and Upload.create_for proceeds anyway, so large-image uploads still fail with the original error after 5 expensive imagemagick invocations blocking the request.

adjudication.rationale: The diff hardcodes `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` in `utilities.js` both for the general client-side size check (replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`) and for the 413 error message (replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`). This means the UI will always tell users the max is 10240 KB and will also enforce a 10MB client-side limit, regardless of the server’s configured `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (or per-type limits). On non-default installs this can misstate policy and can incorrectly block uploads that the server would accept or allow uploads that the server would reject.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] OptimizedImage.downsize is defined twice in optimized_image.rb:143-149; the second 3-arg def silently replaces the original 4-arg version, causing ArgumentError for all existing 4-arg callers (avatar/thumbnail/cooked-image resizing paths crash at runtime)

adjudication.rationale: In optimized_image.rb the diff leaves an existing 4-arg `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and then later adds another `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. Ruby does not overload methods, so the later definition replaces the earlier one. Any existing callers passing (from,to,width,height) will now bind `dimensions=width` and `opts=height` (an Integer), leading to errors when `optimize` does `opts[:allow_animation]` (NoMethodError) or, if callers pass 5 args including opts, ArgumentError for too many args. This is a real runtime-breaking defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The downsize loop in uploads_controller.rb:63-70 calls OptimizedImage.downsize with from == to, destructively overwriting the user's uploaded original in place with no backup; the original full-resolution data is irreversibly lost, and a partial ImageMagick failure can leave a truncated/corrupt file with nothing stored

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)`, so the ImageMagick convert runs with the same input and output path. The diff shows no temp/backup file or atomic rename, and `OptimizedImage.convert_with` can fail (returns false on nonzero exit) but the caller ignores the return value. This can irreversibly clobber/corrupt the only copy of the uploaded data (the tempfile) before `Upload.create_for` reads it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The '80%' geometry in the downsize loop reduces dimensions by 20% per pass, so images can still exceed max_image_size_kb after all 5 attempts, then Upload.create_for is called with an oversized file that fails validation after wasted CPU passes (or gets stored oversized)

adjudication.rationale: The new controller logic tries up to 5 downsizes with geometry "80%" while `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, but then unconditionally calls `Upload.create_for(...)` even if the file is still oversized. It’s true that repeated 20% dimension reductions may still leave very large images above the max after 5 attempts, leading to wasted processing and a likely eventual rejection elsewhere. However, the claim that it “gets stored oversized” or definitively “fails validation” depends on `Upload.create_for` behavior not shown in the diff, so the finding overstates what can be verified here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Hardcoded 10 * 1024 KB client-side and 10.megabytes server-side replace SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb in utilities.js:182, utilities.js:246, and uploads_controller.rb:55, silently ignoring the admin-configurable setting and causing the limits to disagree within the same diff

adjudication.rationale: The diff hardcodes upload size limits to 10MB in multiple places that previously used admin-configurable settings: utilities.js changes maxSizeKB from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to `10 * 1024` and from `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to `10 * 1024`, and uploads_controller.rb changes the API URL download cap from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to `10.megabytes`. This verifiably ignores the configured `max_*_size_kb`/`max_image_size_kb` values and can display/enforce limits that don’t match the actual server-side setting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The downsize loop's animated-GIF handling depends on the tempfile path ending in .GIF, but tempfile paths never end in .gif, so the animated instructions branch can never trigger and large animated GIFs get flattened/handled as static images, destroying animation

adjudication.rationale: In the new upload-size reduction loop (`uploads_controller.rb`), downsizing is invoked as `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)`. In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, the animated branch is selected only when `opts[:allow_animation]` is true *and* `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Because `from` here is the tempfile path (not the original `filename`), and the diff shows at least one tempfile is created with a fixed prefix (`FileHelper.download(..., "discourse-upload-#{type}")`) that does not include an image extension, the animated-GIF detection can fail, causing animated GIFs to be processed by the non-animated instructions (potentially flattening/destroying animation) during this newly added downsizing behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `app/models/optimized_image.rb:145-156` — `def self.downsize` is defined twice in the same class; Ruby keeps the later definition, so callers passing the old 4-parameter signature `(from, to, max_width, max_height)` have the 4th argument (`height`) bound to `opts`, causing `opts[:allow_animation]` to raise `TypeError (no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer)` and crashing every thumbnail/lightbox path that downsizes with explicit width/height.
matched_golden_ids: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying bug: `downsize` is defined twice, and the later definition overrides the earlier one with a different parameter signature. This makes the original (separate width/height) version unreachable and breaks existing callers using `(max_width, max_height)`; the candidate further explains the resulting argument misbinding and runtime TypeError.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-68` — `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` passes the literal string `"80%"` as the `dimensions` argument into `downsize_instructions`/`downsize_instructions_animated`, which expect width/height geometry; the malformed convert command fails, `convert_with` returns `false` which is discarded, all 5 loop attempts run against an unchanged file, and `Upload.create_for` receives the original oversized tempfile with no indication of downsizing failure.
matched_golden_ids: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same core bug: the controller passes "80%" as the resize geometry, but the (especially animated) downsizing path expects WxH-style dimensions, so resizing fails and the upload proceeds without actually being downsized. The candidate additionally notes the failure is silently ignored and retried, which is consistent with the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `app/assets/javascripts/utilities.js:182` — `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB` replaces the per-type server setting `SiteSetting['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, so admin-configured limits are ignored client-side: uploads the server would accept are blocked at 10MB, files between the real server limit and 10MB pass client validation and hit a 413, and the error message at line 246 always states "10 MB" regardless of the actual enforced limit.

adjudication.rationale: The diff hardcodes client-side upload size validation to `10 * 1024` KB in `utilities.js` (both the generic check and the 413 handler), replacing the previous use of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` / `max_image_size_kb`. This demonstrably ignores admin-configured per-type limits and will (a) block uploads >10MB even if server settings allow larger, and (b) always report the limit as 10MB regardless of actual server enforcement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55` — `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` hardcodes the URL-download cap for all types including attachments, ignoring `max_attachment_size_kb`; for large image URLs the download is silently truncated via `rescue nil` and `Upload.create_for` is called with `tempfile == nil`, causing `tempfile.size` to raise NoMethodError and return a 500 instead of a 4xx response.

adjudication.rationale: The diff hardcodes size limits instead of using site settings: in `utilities.js` it replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a fixed `10 * 1024`, and in `uploads_controller.rb` it replaces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` with `10.megabytes` for URL downloads. This concretely ignores configured per-type limits (and `max_image_size_kb`) and can cause incorrect accept/reject behavior versus admin settings. However, the claim about a new 500 due to `tempfile == nil` isn’t verifiably introduced by this diff, since the `rescue nil` pattern and later `tempfile.size` usage existed before; the hardcoding issue itself is still a real defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64-68` — Up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick invocations run inline on the request thread with no timeout, discarded output, and in-place read/write on the same tempfile path; a pathological or adversarial large image can pin a web worker for the duration of 5 unbounded converts, and the API/URL path can reach this loop with arbitrarily large remote files despite the client-side 10MB cap.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an inline downsizing loop in `uploads_controller.rb` that can invoke ImageMagick up to 5 times synchronously on the request thread: `while attempt > 0 ... OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` (in-place read/write). `OptimizedImage.convert_with` executes a shell command via backticks and discards output (`&> /dev/null`) with no timeout or resource bounding shown in the diff. This creates a verifiable DoS/performance risk where a crafted/expensive image can tie up a web worker for multiple unbounded conversions. The finding’s statement about the API URL path allowing "arbitrarily large" remote files is overstated because the download is capped at `10.megabytes` in the diff, but the core risk (blocking, unbounded convert work) is real and introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-68` — The downsize loop's only exit conditions are `attempt == 0` or size satisfied, with no distinction between progress and failure; when 5 iterations of 80% scaling still leave the file above `max_image_size_kb`, the code silently proceeds to upload creation which fails size validation, giving the user a confusing "file too large" error with no indication downsizing was attempted and no log line recording the failure.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb` a new downsizing loop runs up to 5 times (`while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`) and then unconditionally proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` even if the file is still above the configured max. The diff shows no explicit handling/reporting/logging of the “downsizing didn’t get under the limit” case, so users may just get whatever downstream error occurs without knowing downsizing was attempted. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove `Upload.create_for` will fail size validation or that the exact error message will be confusing, so this is more of an incomplete edge-case handling concern than a verifiable defect.
